On Mon, Mar 30, 2020 at 2:39 PM Rebecca G <rebecca.j...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all,

I'm trying to simulate multisession capture histories with equal sex-ratio but male-biased detection. If I had multi-catch traps this would be fine as I can simulate the capthists for each sex and bind them back together but of course this will give me multiple captures at the same trap in the case of single-catch traps. Any opinions on how much of an issue this is or any potential workarounds? 

Once I have two capture histories I'm also struggling binding them together. If I have two capthists of length 10, if I use MS.capthist(ch1, ch2) I'm getting a capthist of length 20. Are there particular arguments I'm missing to deal with this?

Thanks,

Rebecca

messages.subject: Re: Simulating multisession capthist with heterogeneity in detections and single-catch traps
parts:
So this is my ad hoc-ish solution using existing secr functions. It's not tidied up as yet so I've just directly entered population and detection parameters into the functions inside the function.

data_sim <- function(){
  success <- FALSE
  while(!success){
    pop_f <- sim.popn(D = 0.2, 
                      core = grid_traps, 
                      buffer = 100, 
                      poly = land, # drops ACs that fall in water
                      nsessions = 10,
                      covariates = list(sex = c(M = 0, 
                                                F = 1)), 
                      Ndist = "fixed",
                      details = list(phi = 0.9, 
                                     lambda = 2.3, 
                                     movemodel = "exponential", 
                                     move.a = 5, 
                                     edgemethod = "reflect")) # if ACs hit the edge of the island they move back in
    # to keep population size within a reasonable range
    success <- 55 <= dim(pop_f[[10]])[1] & dim(pop_f[[10]])[1] <= 80
  }
  success <- FALSE
  while(!success){
    pop_m <- sim.popn(D = 0.2, 
                      core = grid_traps, 
                      buffer = 100, 
                      poly = land, # drops ACs that fall in water
                      nsessions = 10,
                      covariates = list(sex = c(M = 1, 
                                                F = 0)), 
                      Ndist = "fixed",
                      details = list(phi = 0.9, 
                                     lambda = 2.3, 
                                     movemodel = "exponential", 
                                     move.a = 5, 
                                     edgemethod = "reflect")) # if ACs hit the edge of the island they move back in
    # to keep population size within a reasonable range
    success <- 55 <= dim(pop_m[[10]])[1] & dim(pop_m[[10]])[1] <= 80
  }
  # females
  ch_f_grid <- sim.capthist(traps = grid_traps, 
                            popn = pop_f, 
                            noccasions = 4, 
                            detectfn = "EX", 
                            detectpar = list(g0 = 0.2, 
                                             sigma = 40), 
                            nsessions = 10,
                            renumber = FALSE)
  # males                    
  ch_m_grid <- sim.capthist(traps = grid_traps, 
                            popn = pop_m, 
                            noccasions = 4, 
                            detectfn = "EX", 
                            detectpar = list(g0 = 0.3, 
                                             sigma = 80), 
                            nsessions = 10, 
                            renumber = FALSE)
  # bind capthists together
  ch_grid <- list()
  for(s in 1:10){
    ch_grid[[s]] <- rbind(ch_f_grid[[s]],
                          ch_m_grid[[s]])
  }
  return(list(ch_grid, pop_f, pop_m))
}

'grid_traps' and 'land' attached. I'm trying to use simulations to verify our inferences in a high trap saturation scenario.
